impact.desc.high: the answer can change the data model, a frozen operation of the API contract or what structures the whole code
impact.desc.medium: the answer can change a provisional operation, a process, a schema not frozen yet or a screen
impact.desc.low: the answer only changes a label, a message, a value or an edge case
open.col.subject: Subject
open.col.question: Question
open.info.purpose: List what is still to be decided on this operation.
open.info.content: One point per row, highest impact first: the subject, the hypothesis the code follows meanwhile, the question Q-xxx when it has been asked to the PO.
open.info.why: A table, because every point has the same attributes and is compared with the others.
open.info.source: x-open of the operation, shown again in the open points view.
dir.in: sent: request body, from the front to the API
dir.err: received as an error: error response of the API
legend.release: first release that exchanges it, after the {first} (indicative)
legend.shared: exchanged by frozen and provisional operations: it can only grow
heading: {kind}: {title}
meta.source.hand: {file} and the hand-written pages, generated page
announced.title: Announced additions
announced.info.purpose.operation: List the elements already described in this operation but belonging to a later release.
announced.info.purpose.schema: List the elements already described in this schema but belonging to a later release.
announced.info.content: One row per addition: its release, the addition, where it goes.
announced.info.why: A table, because each addition is a fact dated by its release. It is the only change allowed on a frozen operation ({inv}).
announced.info.read: Before its release, the server does not send the addition and rejects it (400 {code}); the front ignores it.
ep.provisional.title: Provisional contract
ep.provisional.text: Reduced level: roles, entities, processes and schemas sketched, open points. The rest (sequence, examples, detailed error cases) is set at the sprint planning that freezes it.
ep.params.col.name: Name
ep.request.info.content: The path and query parameters, then the body and its schema (↑ sent).
ep.request.info.why: The Parameter and Request Body objects of OpenAPI, rendered as a table. The raw form is in the source file and the Swagger UI view: two views of one source.
ep.responses.info.content: One row per status and per business code: schema of the body, code of {code}, case. The errors common to all operations fit on one line, then come the examples.
ep.responses.info.why: The Responses of OpenAPI and the application/problem+json errors (RFC 9457): one code per row, what is common is not repeated.
ep.responses.info.read: ↓ received, red ↓ received as an error. "+ field": property of {schema} that this code fills in. How the front handles errors is in the error handling.
ep.behaviour.processes.none: none: the logic stays in the endpoint
ep.behaviour.info.purpose: State the facts the code complies with.
ep.behaviour.info.content: One fact per term, from what the operation does to the data it touches.
ep.behaviour.info.why: A definition list: one fact per term, no prose.
ep.behaviour.info.read:
• Checks on the data: those that go beyond the role.
  • Rules: the business rules to test ({inv}).
  • Idempotence: the effect of a second identical call, as defined by RFC 9110.
  • Data: C create, R read, U update, D delete.
ep.sequence.info.purpose: Show the order of the calls between front, API, processes and database, and the transaction.
ep.sequence.info.content: The diagram, with the response of each case, then its identifiers as links.
ep.sequence.info.why: A UML sequence diagram (Mermaid): it shows the flow that the list of facts does not show.
ep.sequence.info.read: The endpoint opens and closes the transaction, a process never does. The diagram holds no link: its identifiers are listed below it.
open.title: Open points
schema.shared.title: Shared by frozen and provisional
schema.shared.text: Exchanged by frozen operations ({frozen}) and provisional ones ({provisional}). The provisional ones can only extend it, in a backward compatible way ({inv}); if they need something else, they take their own schema.
schema.layer: HTTP, JSON body: between the API access service of the front and the route of the API, which validates it
placement.info.purpose: Say where this schema travels: who sends it, who receives it, through which endpoint, in which HTTP message.
placement.info.content: One row per endpoint and per direction, the schema alone or inside another one; the message is the request, or the response with its status.
placement.info.why: A table whose columns never change: the placement reads without ambiguity.
placement.info.read: Direction seen from the front: ↑ sent in the request body, ↓ received in a response, red ↓ received in an error response.
placement.info.source: The screens come from the macro design, the rest from openapi.yaml.
fields.closed: No other field is accepted (additionalProperties: false).
fields.info.purpose: Give the shape of the schema.
fields.info.content: One row per field: type, whether it is required, constraints, description. Nested objects are expanded (a.b, a[].b).
fields.info.why: The readable rendering of the JSON Schema of openapi.yaml. The raw form is in the source file and the Swagger UI view: two views of one source.
format.info.purpose: Give the shape of a schema without properties.
format.info.why: A definition list, readable rendering of the JSON Schema.
example.info.purpose: Give what is needed to write a mock or a test without inventing anything.
example.info.content: A valid instance of the schema.
example.info.source: The example of the schema, else the first example of an endpoint that exchanges it whole.
schema.title: Schema {name}

types.error-codes.one: string, {n} value, described in the error catalog
types.error-codes.other: string, {n} values, described in the error catalog

schemas.exchanged.info.purpose: Find a schema that an endpoint sends or receives directly, and see where it travels.
schemas.exchanged.info.content: One card per domain. On each row: the schema (link to its page), the entity it is a projection of, its description, its placement (direction, endpoints, HTTP status of the response).
schemas.exchanged.info.why: A domain is a file components/schemas/<domain>.yaml: the cards follow how the API contract is split.
schemas.exchanged.info.read: ↑ sent, ↓ received, red ↓ received as an error.
types.info.purpose: Describe the schemas used only inside the exchanged schemas.
types.info.content: One row per type: format, schemas that use it, description, announced additions.
types.info.why: A shared type never travels alone: no page, one row that the pages cite by its anchor (#Day).
types.info.read: An announced enum value carries its release. The front renders a value it does not know as the generic case of the screen ({inv}).
changelog.info.purpose: Follow the versions of the API contract.
changelog.info.content: One entry per version, most recent first, each change preceded by its kind.
changelog.info.why:
Semantic versioning (SemVer), which tells the front whether a version affects it ({inv}):
  • major: breaks a frozen operation, only with an accepted ADR;
  • minor: a frozen addition, or an operation that goes from provisional to frozen;
  • patch: no effect on what is frozen.
changelog.info.source: info.x-changelog, kept by the architect at each sprint planning that freezes or adds.
schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.lede: {exchanged} and {types}, from components/schemas. The whole API contract can also be read in the Swagger UI view.
swagger.failed: Swagger UI could not be loaded (network?). The API contract can be read in openapi.yaml.
swagger.info.purpose: Read the whole API contract in the standard view, raw and tooled.
swagger.info.content: Swagger UI, calls to the endpoints disabled.
swagger.info.why: The second way to read the endpoint and schema pages, in the standard OpenAPI tool.
swagger.info.read: The team's x- extensions are not shown: they are in the pages of the endpoints. The link of an operation (#/tag/operationId) opens on it.
swagger.info.source: openapi.yaml and its files, joined at generation time.
swagger.title: API contract, Swagger UI
swagger.lede: {title} v{version}, {ops}. Read-only view: calls to the endpoints are disabled.
sitemap.gen-page: Page generated from openapi.yaml and the hand-written pages: do not edit, change the source and regenerate
sitemap.legend.family: a family of pages of the same model: its title opens the list of its pages
screen-map.no-preview: no preview in the UX/UI spec
screens.common: Codes common to all screens, handled by the translation service: {codes}.
open.view.info.purpose: Gather everything still to be decided in the detailed design.
open.view.info.content: All open points, highest impact first, then by object: entities, endpoints, processes, cross-cutting pages.
open.view.info.why: A sortable table, because every point has the same attributes and is compared with the others.
open.view.info.read: A question asked to the PO carries its Q-xxx link; "{notAsked}": to ask before the sprint planning that takes the object.
open.view.info.source: Each point is written once, in the page of the object where the answer lands (x-open of an operation, open points table of a hand-written page): the Object link leads there.
open.view.h1: what is still to be decided
open.view.lede: The single view of the open points, from the highest impact to the lowest. The highest is decided first: it can change what is frozen.
